question: A 3-year-old child is assessed at the bedside. He opens his eyes only in response to pain, makes incomprehensible sounds, and withdraws his arm from a painful stimulus. Which of the following BEST describes his neurological status?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This child does NOT respond to voice — he requires a painful stimulus. He is therefore NOT Alert (A) on AVPU. A GCS of 9 would require higher scores in each domain than described.

Correct. He responds only to pain — AVPU = P. GCS: Eyes open to pain = 2, Incomprehensible sounds = 2, Withdrawal to pain = 4; total = 8. A GCS ≤8 conventionally indicates severe impairment of consciousness and warrants airway protection. P on AVPU broadly correlates with GCS ≤8.
He does respond to pain (eye opening, withdrawal), so he is NOT Unresponsive on the AVPU scale. GCS 6 would require lower scores than his actual responses (eye 2, verbal 2, motor 4 = 8).
He requires a painful stimulus to elicit any response, which categorises him as P (Pain) on AVPU, not V (Voice). A GCS of 10 would require at least one domain to score higher than shown.

overallFeedback.feedback: Calculate GCS systematically: Eyes to pain = 2; Incomprehensible sounds = 2; Withdrawal = 4; total = 8. He responds only to pain → AVPU = P. GCS ≤8 / AVPU P or U = severe impairment, requires airway protection and urgent blood glucose check.

Correct. AVPU = P; GCS = 2+2+4 = 8. GCS ≤8 or AVPU = P/U signals severe consciousness impairment. Immediate action: secure airway, check blood glucose (ALWAYS in any unconscious/convulsing child), and position safely.
